recommended_approach: Drive a Mantaflow-style fire setup through Blender’s fluid RNA settings, centering control on the fluid domain and flow settings classes. In particular, use `bpy.types.FluidDomainSettings` for domain-level simulation/detail controls (including domain noise controls like `noise_strength`, `noise_time_anim`, and `noise_type`) and `bpy.types.FluidFlowSettings` for per-emitter/flow controls (including a `noise_texture`). This suggests an approach of: (1) configure the domain via `FluidDomainSettings`, (2) configure the emitter/flow via `FluidFlowSettings`, and (3) add small-scale detail by leveraging the domain/flow noise-related parameters exposed on these types.

domain_settings.noise_strength: (bpy.types.FluidDomainSettings attribute) — increase to boost small-scale detail in the simulated fire/smoke volume without changing base motion.
domain_settings.noise_time_anim: (bpy.types.FluidDomainSettings attribute) — animate/time-offset noise evolution to avoid static-looking detail when slowed down.
domain_settings.noise_type: (bpy.types.FluidDomainSettings attribute) — choose noise mode appropriate to the desired detail character (documentation lists it as a configurable attribute).
domain_settings.flip_ratio: (bpy.types.FluidDomainSettings attribute) — available domain parameter noted in the API index; keep in mind when tuning domain behavior if using FLIP-related setups.

flow_settings.noise_texture: (bpy.types.FluidFlowSettings attribute) — use a texture input to modulate/emphasize fine variation at the source/emitter level (useful for candle-flame wavering and wispy break-up).
